Reports Third Quarter 2026 Net Income of $636 million, up 29% YoY, and EPS of $1.41, up 34% YoY and 8% QoQ ROTCE of 15.1%; Dividend raised 13% Positive Operating Leverage of 5.3% YoY Key Financial Data 3Q26 2Q26 3Q25 Third Quarter 2026 Highlights Income Statement ($s in millions) ■ EPS of $1.41; ROTCE of 15.1% – Continued strong Private Bank progress, contributing $0.16 to EPS ■ PPNR of $929 million, up 4.5% QoQ, up 18.6% YoY – NII up 2.7% QoQ, with NIM up 2 bps to 3.19%; NII up 13% YoY, with NIM up 19 bps – Fees down 1% QoQ reflecting lower Mortgage and Capital Markets, partially offset by record Wealth; up 2.7% YoY – Positive operating leverage of 1.8% QoQ and 5.3% YoY ■ Average loans up 1% QoQ, with growth led by Private Bank and retail; up 0.5% QoQ on a spot basis ■ Credit continues to be broadly favorable; net charge-offs of 37 bps, stable QoQ; ACL coverage of 1.47% ■ Average and spot deposits broadly stable QoQ – Private Bank spot deposits of $18.5 billion, up ~$750 million, or 4%, QoQ – Total deposit costs well controlled, up 3 bps QoQ ■ Strong liquidity profile; We remain confident in our positioning and outlook for Q4 and for 2027.” Citizens also announced today that its board of directors declared a quarterly common stock dividend of $0.52 per share, a $0.06, or 13%, increase compared with the prior quarter. The dividend is payable on November 13, 2026 to shareholders of record at the close of business on October 30, 2026. In addition, Citizens announced today that its board of directors increased Citizens Financial Group, Inc. the capacity of its common share repurchase program to $1.95 billion, an increase of $1.3 billion above the $650 million of capacity currently remaining under the prior June 2025 authorization. reference.summary: Citizens Financial Group, Inc. operates as the bank holding company that provides retail and commercial banking products and services to individuals, small businesses, middle-market companies, large corporations, and institutions in the United States. The company operates through two segments, Consumer Banking and Commercial Banking. The Consumer Banking segment offers deposit products, mortgage and home equity lending products, credit cards, business loans, and wealth management services; and education and point-of-sale finance loans, as well as digital deposit products. This segment serves its customers through telephone service centers, as well as through its online and mobile platforms.
